title: What If Both Engines Quit on Your Plane? ✈️
description:
Both engines stop on the plane Gus is on, seven miles up, and the only thing that stops with them is his movie. This is why an airliner without engines does not fall, and how far it gets.

The numbers:
• A plane's wings hold it up, its engines only push. Without thrust an airliner is a glider: for every mile it sinks it slides about 15 miles ahead (published lift-to-drag ratios of airliners in cruise are 15 to 19; a real engine-out glide is nearer 12 to 17)
• That slope is 3.8 degrees, flatter than the steepest wheelchair ramp the ADA allows (1:12, 4.8 degrees)
• From 38,000 feet (7.2 miles) a 15:1 glide covers 108 miles in still air (86 to 122 miles for 12:1 to 17:1) and takes about 18 minutes at a glide speed of 230 knots
• It has been done: on 24 August 2001 an Airbus A330 that ran out of fuel over the Atlantic glided about 75 miles (65 nautical miles) to Lajes in the Azores in 19 minutes. All 306 people on board lived; 18 were hurt leaving the aircraft
• The little propeller is a ram air turbine: about 80 cm across, it drops into the airstream and drives only the flight controls and the essential instruments
• On a normal flight the descent starts about 3 nautical miles out for every 1,000 feet (the pilots' rule of three): about 130 miles from 38,000 feet, with the engines at or near idle, which is close to a glide
(Assumptions: still air, best glide speed, a runway within reach. Both engines failing at once is extremely rare and is a real emergency; this is what the aeroplane does, not advice.)

Sources:
• Wikipedia, "Lift-to-drag ratio" (cruise L/D of airliners; glide ratio = L/D)
• GPIAA Portugal, final report on Air Transat Flight 236 (2001); AOPA Pilot, "Dead-stick night landing" (2005)
• Wikipedia, "Ram air turbine"; "Rule of three (aeronautics)"; AOPA Pilot, "Turbine Pilot" (1995)
• U.S. Access Board, ADA Standards 405.2 (ramp slope 1:12)
• International Standard Atmosphere, ISO 2533

Every number is computed in code and checked. Animation, narration and music are made with software and AI tools.
